merge_corrections.what: MERGED WITH ONE FINDING RECORDED AND NOT FIXED. Every one of the thirty-two processes carries the same judgment citation - 'Standards-aligned decomposition where the cited authorities do not prescribe a utility workflow or threshold'. It is honest and nothing in it is false, but it is a category disclaimer rather than a statement about any process: a reader who wants to know what is inferred in 12.3.2 specifically learns nothing from it. Across the twelve categories merged before this one, the most any single judgment citation is shared by is three processes out of eighteen, and ten of the twelve never exceed one. The check is now in validate_spec.py as a WARNING rather than an error, because this is a rewrite of thirty-two citation strings and not of the category, and because rejecting a fourth time on a rule discovered at merge would stall work that is otherwise good. It is on the submitter's list as a follow-up pass. NOTHING ELSE WAS CHANGED.
accepted_from_submitter: Ten SPEC processes, and all ten justified correctly - either a standing capability with no instance boundary (12.1.4, 12.2.1, 12.2.6, 12.2.7, 12.3.1, 12.5.3, 12.6.3) or a determination whose rule the pack does not state (12.4.3, 12.5.2, 12.6.2). Health indexing, condition thresholds and consequence-of-failure scoring are precisely the things section I of the pack records as not standardised, and the submission refused to invent them.

12.3 uses PODS 7 for gas linear and inspection entities and says plainly that no linear-referencing or dynamic-segmentation standard is in the pack, rather than borrowing IEC 61968 - which is electric-scoped - to cover a gas main.

12.6.1 cites 49 CFR 192.13(c) for the duty to maintain, modify as appropriate and follow the required plans and procedures, and pairs it with NESC Rule 214A2 as the electric exemplar. That is the gas-leads asymmetry applied to obligations rather than to intervals.
12.2.5 is CMMN and correctly so: a record exception is resolved in an order that depends on which system holds the authority, and two data stewards would not take the same one.
merge_corrections.models_built_here: Nine artifacts, 6 BPMN and 3 CMMN. The specification names them; only this side has the generator.

merge_corrections.what: Corrections-only replacement. The submitter rewrote the judgment citation on all thirty-two processes, replacing one category-wide disclaimer with a per-process statement of what that process infers. Diffed field by field before merging: SOURCES ONLY changed on all 32; intent, activities, trigger, inputs, outputs, systems, interfaces, roles, data objects, controls, measures, variants, notation and en17007 are byte-identical to the merged version. The finding recorded at the first merge is closed - the maximum judgment citation share is now 1 of 32, against a merged-category maximum of 3.
merge_corrections.verification: validate_spec.py: 0 errors, 0 warnings, where the previous file carried 1 warning.

derivation: STANDARDS-DERIVED. Every field traces to a standard, regulation, recognised industry body or explicit judgment. No client or product practice is generalised.
taxonomy_origin: TAXONOMY ORIGIN, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT FACT FROM THE DERIVATION ABOVE. The derivation line describes where FIELD CONTENT comes from: every field value traces to a standard, a regulation or a recognised industry body and carries its citation. It does NOT describe where the taxonomy comes from. Which processes exist, how they are grouped and what they are called is a practitioner synthesis of delivered implementations, generalised until it is product- and client-neutral. Of the 102 process groups, 43 originate in programme material, 28 in domain research, 20 in a published source and 11 in folder and file names; the provenance layer grades every one and names what to read next. This model is DELIVERED PRACTICE SPECIFIED AGAINST STANDARDS, not a standard turned into a model - and saying so is not a weakness. A taxonomy proven in delivery and then held against the standards is a stronger claim than one derived from a standard and never built.
field_set: EN 17007:2017 cl. 5.2 maintenance process profile, corroborated by ISO 9001:2015 cl. 4.4.1 a) to h).
gaps: No asset-information model in the permitted pack spans gas and electric distribution. IEC 61968 is electric-scoped; PODS 7 and UPDM 2026 cover gas asset and inspection data but not the work item.

The shared vocabulary has IEC 61968-6 work payloads but no asset-change payload. Category 12 interfaces therefore use the permitted work messages only where an asset change is tied to work; a cross-commodity asset-change contract remains missing.

No permitted source assigns a system of record by asset class, defines distributed-data federation or replication, or prescribes record-matching and conflict-resolution rules. Processes 12.2.1, 12.2.5 and 12.2.7 state these as governed operator determinations.

No linear-referencing or dynamic-segmentation standard is present in the Source Authority Pack. PODS supplies gas linear and inspection entities, but route calibration, measure conversion and event reattachment rules remain unsourced across commodities.

No standard in the permitted pack defines distribution asset condition assessment, a health index, likelihood and consequence scoring, replacement thresholds or portfolio optimisation. Processes 12.4.3, 12.6.2 and 12.6.3 remain SPEC rather than invented DMN models.

No permitted source defines predictive or prescriptive maintenance analytics, a cross-commodity job-plan content set, or a utility warranty-claim workflow. Processes 12.5.2, 12.5.3 and 12.5.5 retain the accountable controls and leave local rules unstated.

GFMAM subject 5.5 Configuration Management remains partial. The category maintains specifications and as-built records but has no explicit configuration baseline, status accounting or version-control process for the asset configuration.
GFMAM subject 6.3 Integrated Reliability remains partial. Failure and performance analysis sit in 12.4, but no explicit reliability-engineering feedback process returns requirements to asset design.

Process 12.1.6 is named Retire and dispose of assets, but category 19.0 now owns physical decommissioning, waste, disposal and transfer. In this specification 12.1.6 retires the record; the process name and boundary remain misleading.

APQC PCF Utilities v7.2.1 process 10.3.1 Plan asset maintenance (pcf_id 19239) spans groups 12.4 and 12.5 plus work-lifecycle groups. Its coarser boundary does not justify moving or merging any assigned process.

processes.name: Control asset-related technical change

group.name: Manage asset risk and compliance obligations

processes.intent: Control asset-related technical change from reason and impact review through records and operating handover.
activities: Register the proposed change, reason and affected assets
Assess technical, risk, work and operating implications
Obtain the required decision and implement through authorised work
Verify records, communication and effective configuration at closure

trigger.text: A proposed temporary or permanent technical change affects an asset, its operation or maintenance basis.

inputs.what: Proposed change, reason and affected assets
Current asset configuration and maintenance basis

outputs.what: Approved, rejected or revised change disposition
Updated effective asset and maintenance records

controls.text: Record reason, authority, implications, required permits, communication, time limits and qualifications where applicable.
